# MimOS boot menu.
#
# GRUB has no font fallback and cannot render an SVG. Every font and image
# named here is a real file installed beside this one, generated by
# scripts/generate-grub-theme.py from packages/mimos-branding/palette.json.
#
# The shape was chosen by David and Jan on 2026-08-10 from four candidates
# booted in real GRUB (docs/evidence/grub/menu/). It is deliberately quiet: no
# card, no wordmark, no slogan, no big logo. What is left is the list, an icon
# per entry, and the countdown.
#
# Rules this file exists to keep, all of them learned from a capture rather
# than from reading:
#
# 1. The background keeps its aspect ratio. A boot menu meets whatever
#    resolution the firmware gives it, and stretching 16:9 artwork onto a
#    16:10 panel distorts everything on it.
# 2. item_spacing must clear 2 x the highlight's corner slice. GRUB draws the
#    selection item_height tall PLUS its corner at each end, so a tighter
#    pitch puts the pill over the entry below. It happened to the old card
#    (ADR-076) and again to the first candidate render.
# 3. The menu box must be tall enough for MORE entries than the machine
#    happens to have. GRUB does not scroll: it silently stops drawing the rows
#    that do not fit, and the first casualty is whatever the generators put
#    last -- measured, that was the firmware-settings entry.
# 4. The screen that follows the menu is deliberately BLACK, and reaching it
#    takes the terminal geometry below and NO bound background (ADR-157).
#    ADR-125 measured the three outcomes: geometry plus an image gives the
#    menu's own artwork, an image without the geometry gives a black
#    rectangle painted over that artwork, and geometry without an image
#    gives a plain black screen. The third is what MimOS wants now, because
#    Windows' boot manager draws only its spinner and never clears what is
#    underneath -- with our artwork bound, choosing Windows meant eleven
#    seconds of MimOS background with a Windows spinner on it, filmed on
#    David's laptop. Do not re-add background_image here to "fix" the black:
#    the black is the fix.

title-text: ""
desktop-image: "background.png"
desktop-image-scale-method: "crop"
desktop-image-h-align: "center"
desktop-image-v-align: "center"
desktop-color: "#221B3A"

# The console GRUB draws on once the menu is gone, while the kernel and the
# initramfs are read. Full screen and nothing bound behind it, which is what
# makes that screen a plain black one rather than a black rectangle painted
# over the menu's artwork -- see rule 4 above. Nothing in this package binds
# a console background any more, and a contract rejects any file that starts
# to (ADR-157).
terminal-left: "0"
terminal-top: "0"
terminal-width: "100%"
terminal-height: "100%"
terminal-border: "0"
# Monospaced, and not the brand's face, because gfxterm is a character-cell
# terminal: it places every glyph in a box of the same width. A proportional
# face there spaces the narrow letters wrong -- MimOS rendered as "Mi mOS" on
# a real machine, which is how this was found. Unifont is what GRUB already
# loads for its own console, so this costs no new artifact.
#
# The menu keeps Baloo 2. That is where the brand belongs and where GRUB
# draws free text rather than a grid.
terminal-font: "Unifont Regular 16"

+ boot_menu {
  left = 26%
  top = 24%
  width = 48%
  height = 58%

  item_font = "Baloo 2 Regular 28"
  item_color = "#F8F4FF"
  # The same colour selected as unselected, on purpose. The pill and the edge
  # already say which row is current, and lifting the text to pure white on
  # top of them is a third signal for one fact. Measured rather than argued:
  # with #FFFFFF here the packaged theme differed from the approved render by
  # 596 pixels, all of them inside the selected entry's own word.
  selected_item_color = "#F8F4FF"
  item_height = 56
  item_spacing = 44
  item_padding = 0

  # The icons GRUB draws from icons/<class>.png. The classes were measured off
  # the generators rather than assumed: 10_linux builds its first class from
  # the first word of GRUB_DISTRIBUTOR lowercased, giving `mimos`, and
  # 30_os-prober does the same with the detected label, giving `windows`. The
  # advanced-options submenu and grub-btrfs's carry no class at all, so they
  # get no icon -- which is what David asked for and what the generators
  # already did.
  item_icon_space = 24
  icon_width = 64
  icon_height = 64

  selected_item_pixmap_style = "select_*.png"
}

+ label {
  id = "__timeout__"
  # «Arrancando en 1 segundos», filmado en el portátil de David el
  # 2026-08-23. GRUB sustituye un %d en una cadena fija y no sabe de
  # plurales: no hay forma de escribir «1 segundo» y «5 segundos» con una
  # sola plantilla. Así que la unidad se abrevia, que en una cuenta atrás
  # es natural en castellano y es correcta para todos los números.
  text = "Arrancando en %d s"
  left = 0
  top = 86%
  width = 100%
  align = "center"
  font = "Baloo 2 Regular 28"
  color = "#B6ADCE"
}
